name: Absolute Error
description: Learn about Absolute Error and its applications in physics.

content.overview: You measure a table and get 99.5 cm, but it's actually 100 cm. How far off were you? That's absolute error—just the plain, no-nonsense gap between what you measured and what's actually true. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: It's always positive—we only care about the size of the gap, not the direction
It keeps the same units as the original measurement (cm, kg, s, etc.)
Example: true value 100 cm, measured 99.5 cm → absolute error = 0.5 cm
content.whyItMatters: Absolute error is the foundation every other error calculation builds on. Before you can figure out how big a mistake really is (relative error) or express it as a percentage, you first need this raw, honest number: exactly how far off your measurement landed.
